name: Can you open a kitchen without losing too much storage?

mainEntity.name: How do you make a kitchen open to the living room without losing cabinet and pantry storage?
mainEntity.text: How do you make a kitchen open to the living room without losing cabinet and pantry storage?

acceptedAnswer.text: One of the biggest mistakes in open-floor-plan conversions is removing storage without replacing it. Once walls disappear, upper cabinets, tall pantry walls, and appliance niches often disappear too. A good design solves that by relocating storage to an island, a dedicated pantry cabinet, a taller refrigerator surround, or custom built-ins in the dining or living zone. Before demolition, homeowners should map where cookware, small appliances, cleaning items, and bulk pantry goods will live after the remodel. In smaller Los Angeles homes, this becomes especially important because open plans can look spacious but function poorly if storage is not planned early. The smartest approach is to design storage before finalizing the opening size.
acceptedAnswer.description: Openings can reduce wall space for upper cabinets, pantries, and appliances, so storage has to be replaced with islands, taller pantry runs, banquettes, or built-ins in other parts of the room.
